docs.title: Walkie SDK
docs.text:
A pure Python SDK for controlling Walkie robots with pluggable protocol support.

Choose between WebSocket (ROSBridge), Zenoh, or mix-and-match per subsystem. No ROS 2 installation required on the client machine.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Protocol-agnostic -- switch between rosbridge and zenoh without changing application code
  • Multi-camera -- head camera over Zenoh, wrist camera over USB, all through a unified API
  • Full robot control -- navigation, dual-arm manipulation, gripper, visualization
  • Zero ROS 2 dependency -- runs on any Python 3.11+ machine

docs.title: Quick Install
docs.text: uv add walkie-sdk

docs.title: 10-Line Quick Start
docs.text:
from walkie_sdk import WalkieRobot

bot = WalkieRobot(ip="192.168.1.100")

# Read telemetry
pose = bot.status.get_pose()
print(f"Robot at ({pose['x']:.2f}, {pose['y']:.2f})")

# Get a camera frame
frame = bot.camera.get_frame()

# Navigate
bot.nav.go_to(x=2.0, y=1.0, heading=0.0)

bot.disconnect()

docs.title: USB Camera Test
docs.text:
The USB camera example also serves as a diagnostic tool:

# Auto-detect first available USB camera
uv run python examples/example_usb_camera.py

# Specify a device by stable path
uv run python examples/example_usb_camera.py /dev/v4l/by-id/usb-Logitech_C920-video-index0

# Specify by device index
uv run python examples/example_usb_camera.py 0

Controls: q to quit, s to save a snapshot.

docs.title: Connection Errors
docs.text:
ConnectionError: Connection timeout after 10.0s.
Is ROSBridge running at 192.168.1.100:9090?
  1. Verify robot IP is reachable: ping 192.168.1.100
  2. Check ROSBridge is running: ros2 node list | grep rosbridge
  3. Check firewall allows the port (9090 for rosbridge, 7447 for zenoh)
  4. Try increasing timeout: WalkieRobot(ip="...", timeout=30.0)

docs.title: No Camera Frames
docs.text:
Camera connection failed: ...
Camera will not be available.
  1. Verify the camera server is running on the robot
  2. Check the port is accessible (8554 for WebRTC, 7447 for Zenoh)
  3. Disable camera if not needed: camera_protocol="none"
  4. Check bot.camera is not None before calling get_frame()

docs.title: No Odometry Data
docs.text:
bot.status.get_pose()  # Returns None
  1. Wait for the first odometry message (may take 100-200ms after connect)
  2. Check the robot is publishing odometry: ros2 topic echo /odom
  3. Verify the namespace is correct if using one

docs.title: USB Camera Not Found
docs.text:
Failed to open USB camera device: /dev/v4l/by-id/usb-...
  1. Check the device exists: ls /dev/v4l/by-id/
  2. Check permissions: ls -la /dev/video*
  3. Add your user to the video group: sudo usermod -aG video $USER (then re-login)
  4. Try a different device path or index
  5. Test with the diagnostic script: uv run python examples/example_usb_camera.py

docs.title: USB Camera Permission Denied
docs.text:
[USBCamera] Device /dev/video0: reconnection failed

On Linux, video devices require membership in the video group:

sudo usermod -aG video $USER
# Log out and back in for the change to take effect

docs.title: Protocol Not Implemented
docs.text:
ValueError: Unknown ROS protocol: ...

Valid values:

  • ros_protocol: "rosbridge", "zenoh", "auto"
  • camera_protocol: "webrtc", "zenoh", "shm", "usb", "none"

docs.title: Arm Actions Fail
docs.text:
[Arm] Action go_to_pose failed: ...
  1. Check MoveIt is running on the robot
  2. Verify the group_name matches your robot config (e.g., "left_arm", "right_arm")
  3. Check joint state subscription is active: bot.arm.get_joint_states() should return data
  4. For custom IK mode, verify the IK solver node is subscribed to the target pose topic

docs.title: Mixed Camera: One Camera Fails
docs.text:
When using the cameras dict, each camera connects independently. If one camera fails, the others still work:

Warning: Camera 'wrist' connection failed: ...
Camera 'wrist' will not be available.

The failed camera returns None from get_frame(). Check which cameras are active:

for name in bot.cameras.camera_names:
    frame = bot.cameras.get_frame(name)
    print(f"{name}: {'OK' if frame is not None else 'No frame'}")

docs.title: Camera(transport)
docs.text:
Robot camera interface.

Wraps a camera transport to provide a consistent API for accessing video frames regardless of the underlying protocol.

This class works with any transport that implements CameraTransportInterface, making it protocol-agnostic (works with WebRTC, ROS Image topics, Zenoh, etc.).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default transport CameraTransportInterface

Camera transport instance implementing CameraTransportInterface

required Example 
frame = bot.camera.get_frame()
if frame is not None:
    cv2.imshow("Robot Camera", frame)
    cv2.waitKey(1)

docs.title: get_frame()
docs.text:
Get the latest camera frame.

Returns the most recent frame received from the camera. Does not block waiting for a new frame - returns the cached frame or None if no frame is available yet.

Returns:

Type Description Optional[ndarray]

BGR image as numpy array (HxWx3, uint8), or None if no frame available

Example 
frame = bot.camera.get_frame()
if frame is not None:
    # Frame is OpenCV-compatible BGR numpy array
    height, width, channels = frame.shape
    cv2.imwrite("snapshot.jpg", frame)

docs.title: Factory & Protocols
docs.text: Transport factory and protocol enums for advanced usage.

docs.title: ROSProtocol
docs.text:
Bases: Enum

Available ROS communication protocols.

Each protocol has different requirements and trade-offs: - ROSBRIDGE: WebSocket via roslibpy. No ROS2 needed on client. Higher latency. - ZENOH: Zenoh DDS bridge. Good performance. No ROS2 needed on client. - AUTO: Auto-detect best available protocol.

docs.title: CameraProtocol
docs.text:
Bases: Enum

Available camera stream protocols.

  • WEBRTC: WebRTC stream. Pairs with rosbridge. Low latency video.
  • ZENOH: Zenoh video stream. Pairs with zenoh transport.
  • SHM: Shared memory. Direct access for same-host scenarios.
  • NONE: Disable camera functionality.

docs.title: TransportFactory
docs.text:
Factory for creating transport instances based on protocol selection.

Uses lazy loading to only import the required transport implementation, avoiding unnecessary dependencies when using a specific protocol.

docs.title: MultiCamera(transport)
docs.text:
Multi-camera robot interface.

Provides convenient access to multiple cameras on the robot: - Head/front camera: Main forward-facing camera - Left wrist camera: Camera on left arm gripper - Right wrist camera: Camera on right arm gripper

This class can wrap either: - A multi-camera transport implementing MultiCameraTransportInterface (e.g. MultiSharedMemoryCamera, ZenohCamera with multi_camera=True) - A single-camera transport implementing CameraTransportInterface (e.g. WebRTCCamera, SharedMemoryCamera) - A dictionary of single-camera transports

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default transport Union[CameraTransportInterface, MultiCameraTransportInterface, Dict[str, CameraTransportInterface]]

Camera transport or dict of camera transports

required Example 
# Get all frames
frames = bot.cameras.get_all_frames()
for name, frame in frames.items():
    cv2.imshow(f"Camera: {name}", frame)

# Get specific camera
head_frame = bot.cameras.get_frame("head")

docs.title: WalkieRobot
docs.text: Main entry point for the Walkie SDK. Wraps all robot subsystems into a single object.

docs.title: WalkieRobot(ip, ros_protocol='rosbridge', ros_port=9090, camera_protocol='webrtc', camera_port=8554, timeout=10.0, namespace='', arm_mode='custom_ik', arm_target_pose_topic='/target_pose', ws_port=None, webrtc_port=None, enable_camera=True)
docs.text:
Main SDK class for controlling a Walkie robot.

Auto-connects to the robot on initialization and provides access to: - .nav: Navigation controls (go_to, cancel, stop) - .status: Telemetry data (get_pose, get_velocity) - .camera: Camera frames (get_frame) - if enabled - .viz: Visualization markers for RViz2 (draw_marker, clear_markers)

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default ip str

Robot IP address or hostname

required ros_protocol str

ROS communication protocol to use: - "rosbridge": WebSocket via roslibpy (default, no ROS2 required) - "zenoh": Zenoh DDS bridge (no ROS2 required) - "auto": Auto-detect best available protocol

'rosbridge' ros_port int

Port for ROS transport (default: 9090 for rosbridge)

9090 camera_protocol str

Camera stream protocol to use: - "webrtc": WebRTC stream (default, pairs with rosbridge) - "zenoh": Zenoh video stream (pairs with zenoh) - "shm": Shared memory (same-host only) - "none": Disable camera functionality

'webrtc' camera_port int

Port for camera stream (default: 8554 for WebRTC)

8554 timeout float

Connection timeout in seconds (default: 10.0)

10.0 namespace str

ROS namespace for topics/actions (default: "" = no namespace)

'' arm_mode str

Default arm control mode: - "moveit": MoveIt motion planning (default) - "custom_ik": Publish Pose to custom IK solver for teleop

'custom_ik' arm_target_pose_topic str

Topic for custom IK mode (default: "/target_pose")

'/target_pose'

Raises:

Type Description ConnectionError

If connection to robot fails

ValueError

If invalid protocol specified

Example 
from walkie_sdk import WalkieRobot

# Default: WebSocket + WebRTC (no ROS2 needed on client)
bot = WalkieRobot(ip="192.168.1.100")

bot.status.get_pose()
# {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0, 'heading': 0.0}

bot.nav.go_to(x=2.0, y=1.0, heading=0.0)
# 'SUCCEEDED'

bot.disconnect()

# With namespace:
bot = WalkieRobot(ip="192.168.1.100", namespace="robot1")
# Topics will be /robot1/odom, /robot1/cmd_vel, etc.

docs.title: Robot-Side Requirements
docs.text:
The robot must run ROS 2 with the appropriate servers depending on your protocol choice:

Component Port Required For rosbridge_server 9090 ros_protocol="rosbridge" WebRTC camera server 8554 camera_protocol="webrtc" Zenoh router 7447 ros_protocol="zenoh" Nav2 stack -- Navigation (bot.nav) MoveIt / IK solver -- Arm control (bot.arm) 
# Example: launch rosbridge
ros2 launch rosbridge_server rosbridge_websocket_launch.xml

# Example: launch with combined bringup
ros2 launch walkie_bringup robot_server.launch.py

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: This guide walks through connecting to a robot and using each module.

docs.title: 1. Connect
docs.text:
from walkie_sdk import WalkieRobot

bot = WalkieRobot(ip="192.168.1.100")

This auto-connects using the default protocols (rosbridge + WebRTC camera). See Protocol Selection for other options.

docs.title: 2. Read Telemetry
docs.text:
pose = bot.status.get_pose()
if pose:
    print(f"Position: ({pose['x']:.2f}, {pose['y']:.2f})")
    print(f"Heading: {pose['heading']:.2f} rad")

velocity = bot.status.get_velocity()
if velocity:
    print(f"Speed: {velocity['linear']:.2f} m/s")

docs.title: 3. Camera
docs.text:
import cv2

frame = bot.camera.get_frame()
if frame is not None:
    cv2.imshow("Camera", frame)
    cv2.waitKey(1)

For multiple cameras, see Camera Setup:

frames = bot.cameras.get_all_frames()
for name, frame in frames.items():
    cv2.imshow(name, frame)

docs.title: 4. Navigate
docs.text:
# Blocking -- waits until the robot arrives
result = bot.nav.go_to(x=2.0, y=1.0, heading=0.0)
print(result)  # "SUCCEEDED" or "FAILED"

# Non-blocking -- returns immediately
bot.nav.go_to(x=5.0, y=3.0, heading=1.57, blocking=False)
print(bot.nav.status)  # "IN_PROGRESS"

# Emergency stop
bot.nav.stop()

docs.title: 5. Arm Control
docs.text:
# Move arm to a Cartesian pose (Euler angles)
bot.arm.go_to_pose(
    group_name="left_arm",
    x=0.38, y=0.19, z=0.58,
    roll=-1.57, pitch=0.0, yaw=1.57,
)

# Read joint states
states = bot.arm.get_joint_states()
print(states["left_arm"]["positions"])

# Control gripper
bot.arm.control_gripper("left_gripper", position=0.7)  # close

See Arm Control Guide for full details.

docs.title: 6. Visualization
docs.text:
from walkie_sdk import SPHERE

# Draw a marker in RViz2
marker_id = bot.viz.draw_marker(
    position=[1.0, 2.0, 0.0],
    quaternion=[0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0],
    marker_type=SPHERE,
    color=[0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.8],
)

# Draw an axis triad
bot.viz.draw_axis(
    position=[0.5, 0.0, 0.3],
    quaternion=[0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0],
    axis_name="target",
)

See Visualization Guide for full details.

docs.title: 7. Disconnect
docs.text:
bot.disconnect()

Or use a context manager for automatic cleanup:

with WalkieRobot(ip="192.168.1.100") as bot:
    bot.nav.go_to(x=2.0, y=1.0, heading=0.0)
    # auto-disconnects on exit

docs.title: Arm Control
docs.text: The SDK provides dual-arm control with joint-level commands, Cartesian (IK) pose control, and gripper manipulation. Access via bot.arm.

docs.title: Control Modes
docs.text:
The arm supports two control modes for Cartesian pose commands:

Mode Value Description MoveIt "moveit" Motion planning via MoveIt action servers. Blocking, with path planning. Custom IK "custom_ik" Publishes PoseStamped to a custom IK solver node. Low-latency, for teleop.

Set the default mode at construction:

bot = WalkieRobot(
    ip="192.168.1.100",
    arm_mode="custom_ik",  # or "moveit"
)

Or change it at runtime:

bot.arm.default_mode = "moveit"

docs.title: Joint Position Control
docs.text:
Send joint positions directly. Each arm has 7 joints:

# Set left arm joint positions (7 values in radians)
bot.arm.set_joint_positions(
    left_arm=[0.0, -0.5, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.5, 0.0],
)

# Set both arms + grippers
bot.arm.set_joint_positions(
    left_arm=[0.0, -0.5, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.5, 0.0],
    right_arm=[0.0, 0.5, 0.0, -1.0, 0.0, -0.5, 0.0],
    left_gripper=0.7,   # 0.0-1.0
    right_gripper=0.0,
)

docs.title: Reading Joint States
docs.text:
states = bot.arm.get_joint_states()
if states:
    print(states["left_arm"]["positions"])    # [7 floats]
    print(states["left_arm"]["velocities"])   # [7 floats]
    print(states["left_arm"]["torques"])      # [7 floats]
    print(states["left_gripper"])             # float or None
    print(states["right_gripper"])            # float or None

docs.title: Cartesian Pose Control (Euler)
docs.text:
Move an arm end-effector to a Cartesian pose using Euler angles:

result = bot.arm.go_to_pose(
    group_name="left_arm",
    x=0.38, y=0.19, z=0.58,
    roll=-1.57, pitch=0.0, yaw=1.57,
    cartesian_path=False,  # True for linear path (MoveIt only)
    blocking=True,
)
print(result)  # "SUCCEEDED" or "FAILED"

In custom_ik mode, the Euler angles are converted to a quaternion and published to the target pose topic. The group_name, cartesian_path, and blocking parameters are ignored.

docs.title: Cartesian Pose Control (Quaternion)
docs.text:
When you already have quaternion data (e.g., from a tracking system):

result = bot.arm.go_to_pose_quaternion(
    group_name="left_arm",
    x=0.38, y=0.19, z=0.58,
    qx=0.0, qy=0.707, qz=0.0, qw=0.707,
    blocking=True,
)

docs.title: MoveGroup Action Interface
docs.text:
For direct MoveGroup action server integration with full constraint control:

result = bot.arm.go_to_pose_quaternion_move_action(
    group_name="left_arm",
    x=0.38, y=0.19, z=0.58,
    qx=0.0, qy=0.707, qz=0.0, qw=0.707,
    link_name="left_link7",
    frame_id="base_footprint",
    allowed_planning_time=10.0,
)

docs.title: Relative Pose Movement
docs.text:
Move relative to the current pose:

result = bot.arm.go_to_pose_relative(
    group_name="left_arm",
    x=0.05, y=0.0, z=-0.02,  # move 5cm forward, 2cm down
    roll=0.0, pitch=0.0, yaw=0.0,
)

docs.title: Home Position
docs.text:
Move an arm to its predefined home position:

bot.arm.go_to_home("left_arm")
bot.arm.go_to_home("right_arm")

docs.title: Gripper Control
docs.text:
# Close gripper
bot.arm.control_gripper("left_gripper", position=0.7)

# Open gripper
bot.arm.control_gripper("left_gripper", position=-15.71)

Note

Gripper position values depend on your robot's gripper hardware. The values above are examples -- check your robot's configuration.

docs.title: Per-Call Mode Override
docs.text:
Override the default control mode for a single call:

# Instance default is custom_ik, but use moveit for this call
result = bot.arm.go_to_pose(
    group_name="left_arm",
    x=0.38, y=0.19, z=0.58,
    roll=-1.57, pitch=0.0, yaw=1.57,
    mode="moveit",  # override for this call only
)

docs.title: Custom IK Topic
docs.text:
The target pose topic for custom IK mode defaults to /target_pose. Change it at construction or runtime:

# At construction
bot = WalkieRobot(
    ip="192.168.1.100",
    arm_target_pose_topic="/my_ik_solver/target",
)

# At runtime
bot.arm.target_pose_topic = "/my_ik_solver/target"

docs.title: Camera Setup
docs.text: The SDK provides flexible camera access through multiple protocols and a unified API. Cameras can come from network streams (Zenoh, WebRTC), shared memory, or local USB devices -- and you can mix them.

docs.title: Single Camera
docs.text:
The simplest setup uses one camera protocol for all cameras:

WebRTCZenohUSBShared Memory 
bot = WalkieRobot(
    ip="192.168.1.100",
    camera_protocol="webrtc",
    camera_port=8554,
)
frame = bot.camera.get_frame()

bot = WalkieRobot(
    ip="192.168.1.100",
    ros_protocol="zenoh",
    camera_protocol="zenoh",
)
frame = bot.camera.get_frame()

bot = WalkieRobot(
    ip="192.168.1.100",
    camera_protocol="usb",
)
frame = bot.camera.get_frame()

bot = WalkieRobot(
    ip="192.168.1.100",
    camera_protocol="shm",
)
frame = bot.camera.get_frame()

docs.title: Multi-Camera (Same Protocol)
docs.text:
When all cameras use the same protocol, use multi_camera=True (Zenoh) or the default behavior of SHM:

# Zenoh multi-camera
bot = WalkieRobot(
    ip="192.168.1.100",
    ros_protocol="zenoh",
    camera_protocol="zenoh",
    multi_camera=True,
)

# Access individual cameras
head = bot.cameras.get_frame("head")
left = bot.cameras.get_frame("left")
right = bot.cameras.get_frame("right")

# Get all at once
frames = bot.cameras.get_all_frames()
# {"head": np.ndarray, "left": np.ndarray, ...}

docs.title: Mixed Camera Transports
docs.text:
When different cameras use different protocols, pass a cameras dict to WalkieRobot. Each key is a camera name, and each value specifies its protocol and configuration:

bot = WalkieRobot(
    ip="192.168.1.100",
    ros_protocol="zenoh",
    ros_port=7447,
    cameras={
        "head": {
            "protocol": "zenoh",
            "topic": "/zed/zed_node/rgb/color/rect/image/compressed",
        },
        "wrist": {
            "protocol": "usb",
            "device": "/dev/v4l/by-id/usb-Logitech_C920-video-index0",
            "width": 640,
            "height": 480,
        },
    },
)

The cameras parameter overrides camera_protocol. Each camera connects independently -- if one fails, the others still work.

docs.title: Accessing Mixed Cameras
docs.text:
# By name
head_frame = bot.cameras.get_frame("head")
wrist_frame = bot.cameras.get_frame("wrist")

# All at once
frames = bot.cameras.get_all_frames()

# Single-camera accessor defaults to "head" (or first camera)
frame = bot.camera.get_frame()

# List available cameras
print(bot.cameras.camera_names)  # ["head", "wrist"]

docs.title: Finding Your Camera
docs.text:
USB cameras are identified by device path. Use stable paths to avoid issues when devices are plugged/unplugged or after reboot:

# List available USB cameras with stable paths
ls /dev/v4l/by-id/
# Example output:
# usb-Logitech_HD_Pro_Webcam_C920_12345678-video-index0
# usb-046d_C922_Pro_Stream_Webcam-video-index0

docs.title: Device Identification Methods
docs.text:
Method Example Stability Device index 0 Fragile -- changes on reboot/replug Device node /dev/video0 Fragile By-id symlink /dev/v4l/by-id/usb-Logitech_C920-video-index0 Stable per device By-path symlink /dev/v4l/by-path/pci-0000:00:14.0-usb-0:2:1.0-video-index0 Stable per USB port

Recommendation

Always use /dev/v4l/by-id/ paths in production. They are stable across reboots and don't change when other USB devices are plugged in.

docs.title: USB Camera Configuration
docs.text:
cameras={
    "wrist": {
        "protocol": "usb",
        "device": "/dev/v4l/by-id/usb-Logitech_C920-video-index0",
        "width": 640,       # optional, camera default if omitted
        "height": 480,      # optional
        "fps": 30,          # optional
    },
}

docs.title: Testing USB Cameras
docs.text:
Use the included test script to verify your USB camera:

# Auto-detect first available camera
uv run python examples/example_usb_camera.py

# Specify a device
uv run python examples/example_usb_camera.py /dev/v4l/by-id/usb-Logitech_C920-video-index0

docs.title: Auto-Retry
docs.text: The USB camera transport automatically retries if the device disconnects. It uses exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, ...) up to 5 attempts by default. Configure via max_retries and retry_base_delay in the camera config.

docs.title: Frame Format
docs.text:
All camera transports return frames in the same format:

  • Type: numpy.ndarray
  • Color space: BGR (OpenCV convention)
  • Shape: (height, width, 3)
  • Dtype: uint8
  • Returns None when no frame is available yet

Frames are always copies -- safe to modify without affecting the internal buffer.

docs.title: Protocol Selection
docs.text: The SDK supports multiple communication protocols. Choose based on your setup.

docs.title: ROS Protocols
docs.text: Protocol ROS 2 on Client Latency Status rosbridge Not required Medium Implemented zenoh Not required Low Implemented auto Not required -- Auto-detects best

docs.title: Camera Protocols
docs.text: Protocol Pairs With Use Case Status webrtc rosbridge Network video stream Implemented zenoh zenoh Network compressed images Implemented shm same-host Shared memory (zero-copy) Implemented usb any Local USB/V4L2 camera Implemented none any Disable camera Implemented

docs.title: Default (ROSBridge + WebRTC)
docs.text:
bot = WalkieRobot(ip="192.168.1.100")
# Equivalent to:
bot = WalkieRobot(
    ip="192.168.1.100",
    ros_protocol="rosbridge",
    ros_port=9090,
    camera_protocol="webrtc",
    camera_port=8554,
)

docs.title: Zenoh
docs.text:
bot = WalkieRobot(
    ip="192.168.1.100",
    ros_protocol="zenoh",
    ros_port=7447,
    camera_protocol="zenoh",
)

docs.title: Without Camera
docs.text:
bot = WalkieRobot(
    ip="192.168.1.100",
    camera_protocol="none",
)

docs.title: Auto-Detect
docs.text:
Tries zenoh first, falls back to rosbridge:

bot = WalkieRobot(
    ip="192.168.1.100",
    ros_protocol="auto",
)

docs.title: Mixed Camera Transports
docs.text:
When different cameras use different protocols (e.g., head camera over Zenoh, wrist camera via USB), use the cameras parameter:

bot = WalkieRobot(
    ip="192.168.1.100",
    ros_protocol="zenoh",
    ros_port=7447,
    cameras={
        "head": {
            "protocol": "zenoh",
            "topic": "/zed/zed_node/rgb/color/rect/image/compressed",
        },
        "wrist": {
            "protocol": "usb",
            "device": "/dev/v4l/by-id/usb-Logitech_C920-video-index0",
        },
    },
)

# Access cameras by name
head_frame = bot.cameras.get_frame("head")
wrist_frame = bot.cameras.get_frame("wrist")
all_frames = bot.cameras.get_all_frames()  # {"head": ..., "wrist": ...}

When cameras is set, it overrides the camera_protocol parameter. The single-camera accessor bot.camera returns frames from the "head" camera (or the first camera if no "head" is defined).

See Camera Setup for more details.

docs.title: Port Configuration
docs.text: Protocol Default Port Parameter rosbridge 9090 ros_port zenoh 7447 ros_port WebRTC 8554 camera_port

docs.title: Backward Compatibility
docs.text:
Legacy parameter names still work:

bot = WalkieRobot(
    ip="192.168.1.100",
    ws_port=9090,           # maps to ros_port
    enable_camera=False,    # maps to camera_protocol="none"
)

docs.title: Visualization
docs.text: The SDK can publish visualization markers to RViz2 for debugging and display. Access via bot.viz, or use the convenience methods directly on bot.

docs.title: Single Marker
docs.text:
from walkie_sdk import ARROW, SPHERE, CUBE

# Red arrow (default)
marker_id = bot.viz.draw_marker(
    position=[1.0, 2.0, 0.0],
    quaternion=[0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0],
)

# Green sphere with custom scale
marker_id = bot.viz.draw_marker(
    position=[3.0, 0.0, 0.5],
    quaternion=[0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0],
    frame_id="map",
    marker_type=SPHERE,
    color=[0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.8],  # [r, g, b, a]
    scale=[0.2, 0.2, 0.2],
)

docs.title: Multiple Markers
docs.text:
ids = bot.viz.draw_markers([
    {
        "position": [1.0, 0.0, 0.0],
        "quaternion": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0],
        "marker_type": ARROW,
        "color": [1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0],
    },
    {
        "position": [2.0, 0.0, 0.0],
        "quaternion": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0],
        "marker_type": SPHERE,
        "color": [0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0],
    },
])

docs.title: Updating Markers
docs.text:
Only pass the fields you want to change. Everything else is kept from the original draw_marker() call:

mid = bot.viz.draw_marker([0, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0, 1])

# Update only position
bot.viz.update_marker(mid, position=[1.0, 2.0, 0.0])

# Update position and color
bot.viz.update_marker(mid, position=[3.0, 0.0, 0.0], color=[0, 1, 0, 1])

docs.title: Deleting Markers
docs.text:
# Delete one marker
bot.viz.delete_marker(marker_id)

# Clear all markers
bot.viz.clear_markers()

docs.title: Marker Types
docs.text:
Import marker type constants from the top-level package:

from walkie_sdk import ARROW, CUBE, SPHERE, CYLINDER, TEXT_VIEW_FACING
Constant Value Description ARROW 0 Arrow pointing along +X CUBE 1 Box SPHERE 2 Sphere CYLINDER 3 Cylinder LINE_STRIP 4 Connected line segments LINE_LIST 5 Independent line pairs CUBE_LIST 6 Multiple cubes SPHERE_LIST 7 Multiple spheres POINTS 8 Point cloud TEXT_VIEW_FACING 9 Billboard text MESH_RESOURCE 10 Mesh from file TRIANGLE_LIST 11 Triangle mesh

docs.title: Publishing Poses
docs.text:
Publish a geometry_msgs/PoseStamped for display in RViz2:

topic = bot.viz.draw_pose(
    position=[1.0, 2.0, 0.0],
    quaternion=[0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0],
)

# Update it later (only changed fields)
bot.viz.update_pose(position=[2.0, 3.0, 0.0], topic=topic)

Use different topics for multiple simultaneous poses:

bot.viz.draw_pose(
    position=[0.5, 0.0, 0.3],
    quaternion=[0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0],
    topic="walkie/target_pose/left_arm",
)
bot.viz.draw_pose(
    position=[-0.5, 0.0, 0.3],
    quaternion=[0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0],
    topic="walkie/target_pose/right_arm",
)

docs.title: Axis Triads
docs.text:
Draw RGB axis arrows (Red=X, Green=Y, Blue=Z) to visualize a coordinate frame:

name = bot.viz.draw_axis(
    position=[1.0, 0.0, 0.5],
    quaternion=[0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0],
    axis_name="ee_target",
    scale=0.15,  # arrow length in meters
)

# Update the axis pose
bot.viz.update_axis("ee_target", position=[2.0, 0.0, 0.5])

docs.title: Convenience Methods
docs.text:
WalkieRobot exposes shorthand methods that delegate to bot.viz:

# These are equivalent:
bot.draw_marker([1, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0, 1])
bot.viz.draw_marker([1, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0, 1])

bot.draw_pose([1, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0, 1])
bot.viz.draw_pose([1, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0, 1])

bot.draw_axis([1, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0, 1])
bot.viz.draw_axis([1, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0, 1])

docs.title: Default Topics
docs.text:
Function Default Topic draw_marker walkie/viz_markers draw_markers walkie/viz_markers_array draw_pose walkie/target_pose draw_axis walkie/viz_axis

All topics respect the robot's namespace setting.
